subject: Interregion latency bridge & customer reconfiguration guidance
messages:
From: CloudZone Ops <ops@cloudzone.net>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Networking anomaly: packet loss affecting us-east-1 and eu-west-2

Jasmine / Jordan,

We're seeing elevated packet loss across two peering fabrics impacting several customers in us-east-1 and eu-west-2. Root cause looks like a configuration mismatch in their router software after a rolling update. We're rolling back the change now; mitigations in progress but we expect residual elevated latency for up to 3 hours for routed traffic.

Affected prefixes: 13.54.0.0/16 (us-east-1), 18.194.0.0/16 (eu-west-2).

I'll follow up with logs and an event link shortly.

— CloudZone Network Ops

Attachment: incident-log-snippet.txt (text)
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: engineering@aisle.co, seth.ramos@aisle.co
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Aug 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Networking anomaly: packet loss affecting us-east-1 and eu-west-2

Hi Seth / Aisle team,

Thanks for the heads up, CloudZone. A quick note to confirm what we're doing on our side and a short set of customer-facing mitigations you can apply immediately to reduce observed latency and errors:

Summary of impact
- Intermittent increased latency and 5xx spike for requests routed through us-east-1 and eu-west-2.
- No evidence of data loss or model state corruption; requests that complete are valid.

Immediate actions we've taken
- Enabled regional routing preference to prefer apac and us-west for traffic originating from Aisle (we've pushed a temporary route policy).
- Flushed KV cache on affected hosts to avoid stale prefix lookups (see attached reroute-commands.sh).
- Activated lower-cost small-model fallback for non-latency-critical routes to reduce token generation time in the affected paths.

Customer guidance / action items for Aisle (recommended, non-blocking)
1) If you control a DNS / edge preference, add a health preference to prefer apac or us-west endpoints for user cohorts in NA / EU until CloudZone confirms full recovery.
2) If you can accept slightly lower embedding dimensionality for background jobs, toggle the background embedding pipeline to v-small for the next 6 hours. We've added a CSV (traffic-preference.csv) with config suggestions for your engineers.
3) Please retain logs from 09:00—12:00 PT and share with ops@cloudzone.net and us if you want us to correlate.

Next steps
- We'll send a formal incident bulletin and a postmortem draft by EOD.
- If you'd like a short live call for walkthrough of the reroute steps, reply with a preferred time.

Apologies for the disruption; we're prioritizing minimal customer impact.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

> 
> Thanks for the heads up, CloudZone. A quick note to confirm what we're doing on our side and a short set of customer-facing mitigations you can apply immediately to reduce observed latency and errors:

Thanks — quick ops check-in:
- I executed the reroute script against the Aisle project and confirmed BGP preference changes propagated to edge pools in ~7 minutes.
- Applied small-model fallback on the public route and validated with synthetic requests (attached output).
- Observed immediate reduction in 5xx rate from 4.2% -> 1.1% for the next-minute sampling window.

Customer action I'd recommend now
- Aisle: If you can, reduce your request concurrency to 6 for the next 90 minutes for endpoints that were hitting us-east-1/eu-west-2. This will smooth queueing while CloudZone finishes rollback.

I'll follow up once CloudZone confirms resolved on their side and will prepare a short technical note for the postmortem.

— Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 23 Aug 2028 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: post-incident summary & request to validate routing preferences

Seth / Aisle team,

CloudZone confirmed rollback at 13:40 PT and reported that control-plane convergence completed by 14:00 PT. The core cause was a misplaced BGP next-hop during their rolling update; they are producing a full vendor postmortem.

What we observed
- Time window: 09:00—14:00 PT 22 Aug 2028
- Symptom: transient packet loss and elevated RTT, manifesting as 5xx errors and delayed token generation for affected routes
- Impacted Redwood endpoints: us-east-1 and eu-west-2 (intermittent)

What Redwood did
- Temporarily shifted Aisle traffic preference to apac/us-west and applied small-model fallback to lower p99 latency on non-leading paths (automated, reversible).
- Cleared KV prefixes to eliminate stale routing entries.
- Monitored token-level latency and error budgets; throttled concurrency as a precaution per Ben's note.

Customer asks and next steps (please reply inline)
- Please confirm you can accept the traffic preference profile attached (traffic-preference.csv) for the next 72 hours. If yes, we'll leave the policy in place and continue monitoring.
- We plan to host a joint postmortem readout Thurs 24 Aug 2028 at 10:00 PT; RSVP if you'd like the ops + network walk-through. Link to draft postmortem: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-postmortem-draft
- Compensation: Our sales ops team is ready to propose a one-time service credit tied to impacted token volume; Jordan / Markus, can you coordinate an offer?

Again, apologies for the disruption. We're focused on preventing recurrence and will share the final postmortem when CloudZone publishes theirs.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Aisle: executive follow-up and credit offer for Aug 22 disruption

Seth / Aisle leadership,

I wanted to follow up personally on behalf of Redwood Leadership. We recognize the outage window on Aug 22 caused measurable disruption to your service; thank you for working through the mitigation steps with the team.

Credit proposal
- Offer: a one-time service credit equivalent to 10% of billed usage for the impacted hourly window (09:00—14:00 PT) applied to your next invoice.
- Next steps: If this is acceptable, we'll raise a credit MCO and route through your procurement contact. Markus (cc) will follow up with an official credit memo.

Operational commitments
- We'll deliver a finalized postmortem (including remediation items) within 5 business days of CloudZone's final report.
- We'll provide an automated healthcheck you can consume (simple webhook) to prefer non-affected regional pools during upstream incidents; Ben will share an implementation playbook.

If you'd like to discuss on a quick call, I'm available tomorrow 09:30—11:00 PT. We value your partnership and will make this right.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
